domain: Religious Law / Political Theology / Commitment System Dynamics
topic_summary: Analysis of the 1890 Manifesto reversing Mormon polygamy practice under US federal pressure. The case examines whether this represents exogenous coercion overriding a religious kernel versus endogenous reinterpretation, and whether the commitment system's revision mechanism functioned or was bypassed.

key_entities: LDS Church (religious authority claiming scriptural mandate for plural marriage)
US Federal Government (territorial sovereign enforcing monogamy via Edmunds-Tucker Act)
Wilford Woodruff (Church President who issued 1890 Manifesto)
D&C Section 132 (1843 revelation establishing polygamy as eternal principle)
Post-Manifesto fundamentalists (splinter groups maintaining original reading)
key_tensions: Divine command vs state law (religious obligation to practice polygamy vs federal criminalization)
Eternal principle vs temporal accommodation (immutable doctrine vs pragmatic suspension)
Prophetic authority vs kernel fidelity (President can revise vs revelation is binding)
key_mechanisms: Edmunds-Tucker Act enforcement (asset seizure, disenfranchisement, imprisonment creating existential threat)
Continuing revelation doctrine (living prophet can receive new revelation superseding prior)
Underground practice continuation (post-Manifesto covert polygamy by leadership 1890-1904)
key_absences: Formal doctrinal renunciation: Manifesto framed as suspension of practice, not error correction of D&C 132
Member consent mechanism: Revision imposed top-down without sustaining vote on doctrinal change

axiom_contradictions.basis: Immutable reading holds that no prophetic authority can supersede an eternal commandment (prophets administer but do not revise divine law); prophetic override reading holds living prophet's authority includes doctrinal revision. No framework holds both: either the law is revisable or it is not.

Immutable reading treats suspension-without-renunciation as illegitimate evasion (practice and doctrine are inseparable for eternal ordinances); temporal accommodation treats suspension as legitimate balancing of competing divine commands. A single framework cannot hold both that the practice is mandatory for salvation AND that its suspension is divinely approved.
